name: Burgruine Schrofenstein
kurzbeschreibung: Burgruine Schrofenstein is boldly perched above the Sanna gorge near Stanz: 12-meter-high keep, ancestral seat of the Knights of Schrofenstein, and free access.
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatically situated Burgruine Schrofenstein is perched on an isolated rocky crag at an altitude of 1,114 meters high above the Landeck basin and the village of Stanz in the Tyrolean Oberland. To the west, the cliff drops almost vertically for more than 150 meters into the wild gorge of the rushing Sanna River. Since the High Middle Ages, this exposed hilltop castle monitored the strategic junction of three central Alpine routes over the Arlberg, the Fernpass, and the Reschenpass. From the secured ruin, a spectacular view opens up over the confluence of the Sanna and Inn rivers, as well as the surrounding three-thousand-meter peaks of the Samnaun Alps and Lechtal Alps.

History & Architecture

First recorded around 1196 as a ministerial castle, the stronghold became the permanent ancestral seat of the esteemed knightly Herren von Schrofenstein around 1220, who served as retainers to the bishops of Chur and the counts of Tyrol. For centuries, the castle functioned as an administrative center and temporary seat of the Stanz regional court. Its most prominent descendant was Christoph von Schrofenstein, who served as Prince-Bishop of Brixen from 1509 to 1521 and played a decisive role in shaping Tyrolean territorial politics. Following the extinction of the male lineage in 1546, the fortress changed hands multiple times (including the Counts of Trautson and the Princes of Auersperg) and decayed into ruins from the 18th century onward. The distinctive landmark of the site is the imposing, approximately 12-meter-high Romanesque-Gothic keep (Bergfried): its massive walls of carefully dressed ashlar masonry have defied the elements for over 800 years. Notable remains of the Gothic palas, sections of the curtain wall, and foundations of former stables and outbuildings are also preserved.

Visit & Getting There

The outdoor grounds and rocky plateau of Burgruine Schrofenstein are freely open all year round and completely free of charge (entry is at your own risk; the tower interior is locked for safety reasons). Getting there by public transport: take ÖBB trains to the Landeck-Zams express station, and from there take VVT bus route 4236 in about 10 minutes up to Stanz bei Landeck (stop Stanz Dorf). From the village center, a scenic, signposted hiking trail leads in about 30 to 40 minutes (approx. 100 meters of elevation gain) through traditional orchards and light mountain forest to the ruin. By car: via the A12 motorway or S16 expressway to the Landeck-West exit, then take the L331 up to Stanz; parking is available on the edge of the village near the community center.

Tips

Due to the narrow, rocky trail with tree roots on the final stretch, the ruin is not wheelchair accessible and unsuitable for strollers; sturdy hiking shoes and surefootedness are required. Stanz bei Landeck is renowned as Austria's first recognized distillery village for its aromatic Stanzer Zwetschken plums (over 50 active schnapps distilleries for barely 600 inhabitants). Be sure to combine your hike to the ruin with a tasting of fine spirits at local Stanz distilleries or a stroll along the historic Stanzer Waalweg irrigation channel trail.
